## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

@AGENTS.md

# Project guide: Atira EHL challenge agent ("From RFQ to bid")

A Python agent that, at run time, uses a model (hosted Qwen) to navigate four websites (tender portal, supplier portal,
ERP, webmail), work out the task from the brief, and submit one answer. Brief: `atira challenge rfq`.
Platform docs: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start and `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md`.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point. Write the agent in `solve(task, page)`. |
| `run.py` | Run contract: `load_run`, `submit_answer`, `seconds_left`. Platform plumbing, change rarely. |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers (CDP); locally starts Chromium. |
| `models.py` | `ask_qwen`, `ask_clef`, `qwen()` (OpenAI SDK client). |
| `agent.json` | Sandbox config: `setup`, `run`, `models` (hosted models to wait for), optional `"browsers": 1-4`. |
| `swarm/`, `agents/` | Agent-swarm framework and one file per agent: see `docs/SWARM.md` (read before adding an agent). |
| `tests/` | Unit tests against fakes. |

`task` has `brief`, `access` (site ids, URLs, credentials), `submission` (`api` or `site`) and `answer_schema`.
For `api` submissions return the answer from `solve()`; for `site` submissions enter it on the website and return `None`.

## Rules that decide whether a submission is accepted

- A model must pick navigation targets and make decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts, crawlers
  or copied values. A coding agent reviews every package. Helpers (parsing, pagination of a model-selected result set,
  validation, form filling) are fine.
- A scored run lasts 20 min. Submit the best answer about 1 min before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`); late = 0.
- Max 4 browsers, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. The sandbox only reaches the platform and the websites.
- Package: max 20 MB compressed, `agent.json` at the root. Never include `.env` or keys (they are git-ignored).
- Hosted models are free, but each call adds simulated cost to ranking (quality, then cost x time). Use Qwen for
  easy steps; first call after idle can take several minutes, so use long timeouts.

## Setup per laptop (once)

Prerequisites: Git, Python is NOT required (uv manages 3.12), and a GitHub account that is on the Atira team.

### Windows (PowerShell)
```powershell
irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # Atira CLI (read the script first if you prefer)
winget install --id astral-sh.uv -e                           # uv
# open a NEW terminal so PATH updates
atira login                                                   # browser sign-in with GitHub
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
```

### macOS / Linux
```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh     # Atira CLI; then add ~/.local/bin to PATH
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh               # uv (or: brew install uv)
# open a NEW terminal
atira login
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium        # on Linux add: uv run playwright install-deps chromium
```

### Both: Claude Code helpers (optional)
```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # lets Claude read run logs, model calls, timings, compare runs
```
Check with `atira whoami`. Use `atira login --device` if no browser is available.

## Develop locally

Two terminals, both in the repo root.

Terminal 1 (leave open): the free-model proxy.
```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2: load scouting env, then run the agent.
```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
```sh
# macOS / Linux
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
`atira scout --env` sets `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, site URLs and the `QWEN_*` / `CLEF_*`
variables pointing at the local proxy. The variables only live in that terminal. Local runs use the public
scouting logins: nothing done there is scored, and answers entered on the tender portal never count. Local model calls
are free and unranked. `atira scout` (no flag) prints the logins and brief for manual browsing.

Unit tests: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -q` (add pytest with `uv add --dev pytest` if missing).

## Test in the real sandbox

```sh
atira test-run . --follow        # same sandbox as scored runs, public dataset, up to 2 h, not ranked
atira test-run . --dry-run       # only shows what would be packed (no upload)
```
Max 3 test runs waiting at once. Inspect results:
```sh
atira status                     # latest submissions and test runs
atira logs <run-id> --follow     # reh_... (test run) or run_... (scored run)
atira package <id>               # what was uploaded
atira cancel <run-id>
```
With the `atira` MCP server Claude can also fetch logs by time, model calls, where time went, browser screens and
compare two runs. Ask it "why did run reh_xxx fail?".

## Run data: save it locally, read it locally first (rule for Claude Code)

The platform (atira CLI and `atira` MCP) is often slow (calls over 2 min) or unreachable, and it keeps only part of a
long log. So every piece of run data that gets pulled is also stored locally in `.swarm/runs/`, and that copy is read
first.

- **Full logs**: `scripts/pull-run.ps1 <run> [-Follow]` writes `.swarm/runs/<run>-log.md` (the whole log, replaced on
  each pull). A Monitor that follows a run also writes the whole stream into that file (`... | tee -a <file> | grep ...`),
  not only the filtered lines.
- **Everything else** (MCP `get_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`, `diagnose_run`, `compare_runs`, what a
  screenshot showed): right after pulling, append it to `.swarm/runs/<run>.md` as a section
  `## <UTC time> - <tool and arguments>` with the result (drop noise, keep scores, errors, timings, key lines).
- **Index**: `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`, one line per run: run id, date, what the package changed, outcome (quality, time,
  answer), main findings. Update it whenever a run is started, ends, or is analysed.
- **Read first**: before calling the platform, check `.swarm/runs/`; call it only for data that is missing there or
  outdated (a run still going). If the platform does not answer, work from the local files and say so.
- **Local runs** (scouting sites, `atira models proxy` running): `scripts/local-run.ps1 -Only "AgentA,AgentB" -Name x`
  runs headless and writes the whole log to `.swarm/local/<time>-<name>.md`. Use them (in the background) to check a
  fix before spending a sandbox test run; note the result in `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md` under "Local checks".
- `.swarm/` is git-ignored and not packaged (`atira test-run . --dry-run` lists it as ignored). The files hold scenario
  values: never copy anything from them into the package.

## Submit (ranked, public)

Run a test run first and make sure it finishes with a valid answer. Then agree in the team who submits
(one submission in flight per team, and it is public and final).
```sh
atira submit . --dry-run         # check the package
atira submit . --follow          # review -> one scored run on the public dataset -> leaderboard
atira leaderboard
```
The final ranking uses a private dataset with different websites and data, so build a general agent that does not
rely on public-dataset specifics. Choose the final attempt with `atira final [--best-of 1|3]` before the final run
starts (own model keys cost up to 3x).

## Models

- Default: hosted `qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, up to 32 concurrent calls/team) via `models.qwen()`; `clef` (image
  decision model, 16 concurrent) via `models.ask_clef`. List every hosted model used in `agent.json` `"models"`.
- Own provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, ...) are stored as team secrets on the team page and go through the run's
  metering proxy. See the run contract, section LLM calls.
- Claude Code (this assistant) is only for writing code and runs on your own Claude. Optional experimental launcher
  `claude-atira` (Windows, per-user setup, not in the repo) points Claude Code at Qwen; plain `claude` is the default.

## Team workflow

See `docs/COLLABORATION.md` (baseline, `scripts/team.py status|sync|integrate`, CI) and `docs/INTEGRATION.md`
(what came from which branch, open contract questions).

- Commit with normal `git commit` / `git push` so Entire checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` branches.
- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys. `.entire/settings.json` is shared; `settings.local.json` is personal.
- Pull before starting, keep commits small, and say in the team chat before running `atira submit`.

## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)

Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.

### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
| Site | Holds | Traps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)
- Quantity = tender qty, overridden by the latest clarification per position; withdrawn answers ignored.
- Requirement = spec revision marked *current*, with scoped amendments applied.
- Material = active ERP material matching bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification EXACTLY; none -> "no bid".
- Price = valid price condition on scenario date at highest reached quantity scale, minus approved discount, round half-up
  to the cent, converted to EUR. Discount = latest sales-director approval for this exact tender (conditional thresholds), else 0%.
- Lead time = stock if it covers qty, else production lead time; shared stock is all-or-nothing per material.
- Konditionsgruppen decide if discount hits base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup fees never discounted.
- Packaging cartons, shared setup/pool fees, delivery commitments allocated per position; project bonus = marginal
  percentage bands allocated proportionally in cents; final price formula rounds ONCE at the end.
- Metal-index rates selected by date; nominal stroke derived from reserves.
- Authority: only authorised senders + exact tender reference; newest valid record wins.
- Partial submission allowed (explicitly omitted positions) but bid must still be signed. Missing material -> no bid.

### Scoring / ranking
- Quality 0-100: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 (minus extra checks), total 5, arithmetic consistency 5;
  +5 each for withdrawn-quantity and metal-index checks when present. Per position: material 20%, quantity 15%,
  base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
- Correct tender reference is mandatory (else ineligible, ranked after all eligible).
- Order: eligible -> quality (higher) -> cost x time (lower; cost = simulated model prices, time = wall clock to accepted answer).
- Final ranking: PRIVATE dataset first, then public, then "system elegance". Private = same jobs/rules/format but different
  software, layouts, names, content, data. Do NOT tune to public-1; derive everything from the sites at runtime.
- Private run uses latest passing submission (or best of 3 if opted in via `atira final --best-of 3`).

### Fair play (an AI reviewer reads the whole package: passed / flagged / rejected)
Forbidden: any scenario value in the package (code, config, prompts, notes, defaults, fallbacks: prices, material numbers,
totals, discounts, tender refs, logins, TANs); pre-solving the answer (yourself or with an assistant) and shipping it;
fixed click paths; crawl-everything-then-one-model-call; model only as fallback; contacting hosts other than platform + 4 sites;
models outside the proxy; local/bundled models; starting own browsers (even headless; extras are killed); attacking platform/sites;
sharing scored-run data. Never write notes addressed to the reviewer (steering counts against us).
Allowed: any agent design, any provider via the proxy with team-secret keys, own code/prompts/tools, OSS libs installed in
`setup`, knowledge from scouting/test runs (as general strategy, never as values), helper code for browser control, parsing,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling, paging through results the model selected.
Helpers MAY NOT discover and traverse the sites to assemble evidence: the model decides where to go, what to search, what matters.

### Building an agent swarm
- Multiple agents/processes/threads are explicitly allowed; no limit on agent count, only **max 4 browsers** (`"browsers": n`
  in `agent.json`, CDP urls in `CDP_URLS`, browser n = display `:n`, CDP port 9221+n). Tabs/contexts inside them are unlimited.
- Frameworks: nothing is whitelisted or banned; any open-source library (respect licence) installed during `setup`
  (network allowed there, no credentials). Toolchains: Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24 (+pnpm, bun, runs .ts), Rust/cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq.
  Run phase is offline except platform + sites + model proxy. Package <= 20 MB. Plain asyncio/threads + OpenAI SDK is enough;
  agent frameworks (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, browser-use, etc.) are fine if they use the proxy base URLs
  and the provided CDP browsers (never launch their own Chromium in scored runs; connect via CDP).
- Suggested shape: an orchestrator (model) that reads the brief and spawns one worker per site / per position
  (tender, spec, ERP, mail run in parallel on separate browsers), workers return structured evidence with source + timestamps,
  a calculator step (plain code, deterministic rounding rules) computes prices, a verifier agent cross-checks authority/dates/
  tender reference/superseded records, then one agent fills the configurator and signs with the TAN.
- Models: hosted `qwen` (32 concurrent, 256k ctx, vision) for navigation/extraction; `clef` (16 concurrent) for quick
  choice/score decisions; use a stronger own-key model only for hard reasoning (cost x time only matters as tie-break after quality,
  so quality first). Every call counts simulated cost, so keep prompts short and use cached prefixes. Warm-up can take minutes: long timeouts.
  List hosted models in `agent.json` `"models"` (`[]` skips warm-up wait).
- All LLM traffic via `$LLM_PROXY_URL` / `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`; send your own User-Agent on platform HTTP calls (default Python UA gets 403).

### Run discipline
- Clock starts at the `run` command; scored 20 min; submit the best answer by ~1 min before end (`run.seconds_left`); late/no answer = 0.
- Build a fallback: keep a best-so-far answer and submit it on a timer even if the swarm is unfinished.
- Submission 400 with `issues` is not final (fix + resend); 202 is final and the process has 10 s to exit.
- Sessions time out (ERP, portals): handle re-login. Prefer partial-correct signed bid over nothing.
- Test runs (2 h, unscored) on public data first; use `atira` MCP (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`) to debug.
  Never copy values from logs/screenshots/answers into the package.

### Links
Challenge: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq · fair play: /docs/fair-play.md · run contract: /docs/run-contract.md ·
API: /docs/api.md · CLI: /docs/cli.md · llms.txt: /llms.txt · leaderboard: /challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md

# Notes for AI coding agents

- This repo is an Atira EHL challenge agent (starter kit). Python 3.12 + uv, Playwright, hosted Qwen via OpenAI SDK.
- Your agent goes in `solve(task, page)` in `agent.py`. `run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py` are platform plumbing.
- `agent.json` defines how the sandbox installs/runs (`uv sync`, `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`) and which hosted models it uses.
- A model must choose navigation/decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts or crawlers (submissions are reviewed).
- Scored run is 20 min: submit the best answer ~1 minute before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`).
- Local run: terminal 1 `atira models proxy`; terminal 2 `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression` then `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`.
- Test in the real sandbox: `atira test-run . --follow`. Ranked submit: `atira submit . --follow` (only when the team agrees).
- The `atira` MCP server is available for debugging runs (logs, model calls, timing).
- Only inspect, save, or reference run data for runs the user identifies as theirs or runs launched for them with a recorded launch receipt. Historical indexes and visible team runs are not proof of ownership. Never collect other teams' run data.
- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys.
- This repo uses Entire: commit your work with normal `git commit` / `git push` so session
  checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` shadow branches manually.

## Working alongside the rest of the team (read docs/COLLABORATION.md)

- `main` is the shared baseline; other developers and their agents work on other branches at the same time.
- **At the start of every task** run `uv run --no-sync python scripts/team.py status --json` and read
  `docs/INTEGRATION.md`. Do not build what already exists in `main` or on another branch; extend it.
- If your branch is behind `main`, run `uv run --no-sync python scripts/team.py sync` (safe: changes nothing unless the
  merge is clean and the tests pass) before editing files that `main` also changed.
- Before changing a file that `status` lists as changed on another branch, say so to the user: it is a likely conflict.
- When two parts must agree (bid rules, result shapes, number formats), extend `tests/test_contracts.py`.
- One task per worktree: `git worktree add ../<task> -b <user>/<task> origin/main`. Never edit another agent's worktree.
- Never commit `.integration/` or `.swarm/`; never force-push; never push to `main` (the integrator moves it).
- [Entire session attach recovery](entire-session-attach-recovery.md) — silent no-op hooks, and how to get a checkpoint back without restarting

## Run data: save it locally, read it locally first (rule for Claude Code)

- **Everything else** (MCP `get_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`, `diagnose_run`, `compare_runs`, what a

## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)

Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.

### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
| Site | Holds | Traps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)
- Quantity = tender qty, overridden by the latest clarification per position; withdrawn answers ignored.
- Requirement = spec revision marked *current*, with scoped amendments applied.
- Material = active ERP material matching bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification EXACTLY; none -> "no bid".
- Price = valid price condition on scenario date at highest reached quantity scale, minus approved discount, round half-up
  to the cent, converted to EUR. Discount = latest sales-director approval for this exact tender (conditional thresholds), else 0%.
- Lead time = stock if it covers qty, else production lead time; shared stock is all-or-nothing per material.
- Konditionsgruppen decide if discount hits base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup fees never discounted.
- Packaging cartons, shared setup/pool fees, delivery commitments allocated per position; project bonus = marginal
  percentage bands allocated proportionally in cents; final price formula rounds ONCE at the end.
- Metal-index rates selected by date; nominal stroke derived from reserves.
- Authority: only authorised senders + exact tender reference; newest valid record wins.
- Partial submission allowed (explicitly omitted positions) but bid must still be signed. Missing material -> no bid.

### Scoring / ranking
- Quality 0-100: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 (minus extra checks), total 5, arithmetic consistency 5;
  +5 each for withdrawn-quantity and metal-index checks when present. Per position: material 20%, quantity 15%,
  base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
- Correct tender reference is mandatory (else ineligible, ranked after all eligible).
- Order: eligible -> quality (higher) -> cost x time (lower; cost = simulated model prices, time = wall clock to accepted answer).
- Final ranking: PRIVATE dataset first, then public, then "system elegance". Private = same jobs/rules/format but different
  software, layouts, names, content, data. Do NOT tune to public-1; derive everything from the sites at runtime.
- Private run uses latest passing submission (or best of 3 if opted in via `atira final --best-of 3`).

### Fair play (an AI reviewer reads the whole package: passed / flagged / rejected)
Forbidden: any scenario value in the package (code, config, prompts, notes, defaults, fallbacks: prices, material numbers,
totals, discounts, tender refs, logins, TANs); pre-solving the answer (yourself or with an assistant) and shipping it;
fixed click paths; crawl-everything-then-one-model-call; model only as fallback; contacting hosts other than platform + 4 sites;
models outside the proxy; local/bundled models; starting own browsers (even headless; extras are killed); attacking platform/sites;
sharing scored-run data. Never write notes addressed to the reviewer (steering counts against us).
Allowed: any agent design, any provider via the proxy with team-secret keys, own code/prompts/tools, OSS libs installed in
`setup`, knowledge from scouting/test runs (as general strategy, never as values), helper code for browser control, parsing,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling, paging through results the model selected.
Helpers MAY NOT discover and traverse the sites to assemble evidence: the model decides where to go, what to search, what matters.

### Building an agent swarm
- Multiple agents/processes/threads are explicitly allowed; no limit on agent count, only **max 4 browsers** (`"browsers": n`
  in `agent.json`, CDP urls in `CDP_URLS`, browser n = display `:n`, CDP port 9221+n). Tabs/contexts inside them are unlimited.
- Frameworks: nothing is whitelisted or banned; any open-source library (respect licence) installed during `setup`
  (network allowed there, no credentials). Toolchains: Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24 (+pnpm, bun, runs .ts), Rust/cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq.
  Run phase is offline except platform + sites + model proxy. Package <= 20 MB. Plain asyncio/threads + OpenAI SDK is enough;
  agent frameworks (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, browser-use, etc.) are fine if they use the proxy base URLs
  and the provided CDP browsers (never launch their own Chromium in scored runs; connect via CDP).
- Suggested shape: an orchestrator (model) that reads the brief and spawns one worker per site / per position
  (tender, spec, ERP, mail run in parallel on separate browsers), workers return structured evidence with source + timestamps,
  a calculator step (plain code, deterministic rounding rules) computes prices, a verifier agent cross-checks authority/dates/
  tender reference/superseded records, then one agent fills the configurator and signs with the TAN.
- Models: hosted `qwen` (32 concurrent, 256k ctx, vision) for navigation/extraction; `clef` (16 concurrent) for quick
  choice/score decisions; use a stronger own-key model only for hard reasoning (cost x time only matters as tie-break after quality,
  so quality first). Every call counts simulated cost, so keep prompts short and use cached prefixes. Warm-up can take minutes: long timeouts.
  List hosted models in `agent.json` `"models"` (`[]` skips warm-up wait).
- All LLM traffic via `$LLM_PROXY_URL` / `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`; send your own User-Agent on platform HTTP calls (default Python UA gets 403).

### Run discipline
- Clock starts at the `run` command; scored 20 min; submit the best answer by ~1 min before end (`run.seconds_left`); late/no answer = 0.
- Build a fallback: keep a best-so-far answer and submit it on a timer even if the swarm is unfinished.
- Submission 400 with `issues` is not final (fix + resend); 202 is final and the process has 10 s to exit.
- Sessions time out (ERP, portals): handle re-login. Prefer partial-correct signed bid over nothing.
- Test runs (2 h, unscored) on public data first; use `atira` MCP (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`) to debug.
  Never copy values from logs/screenshots/answers into the package.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: scraper   SITE: webmail (role "mail")
"""Reads the mails that matter for this tender, saved as page evidence ("mail.page").

Every message is read once:
1. The main tab logs in while the brief is being read.
2. Index pass (main tab): one search for the exact tender reference alone, in inbox and archive; the model picks the
   messages about this tender from the result lists and reads them all with read_page(urls=[...]). Then
   results["done.mail_core"] (the discount analyst starts).
3. The analyst's extraction says which topics the brief names (authorised senders: discount approval, condition
   rules, technical release, packaging, ...) have no valid message yet. Only those get a topic search, in parallel
   tabs (each logs in: this webmail keeps its login per tab). Messages already saved by another agent are not opened
   again (read_page returns the saved text). Then results["done.mail"].
The signing TAN is NOT read here: the submitter asks for it when it signs (agents/submit_bid.py)."""
import os
import asyncio

from agents.analyze_discount import covered_topics, refresh
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
from swarm import Phase, register  # noqa: F401
from swarm.scraper import SiteScraper
from swarm.sites import site_for

TOPIC_TABS = int(os.environ.get("SWARM_MAIL_TABS", "2"))   # parallel mail topic tabs; was 3 (sandbox CPU)

SEARCH_RULES = (
    "Mailbox search combines words with AND and shows limited hits. Look-alike references (same reference with "
    "suffix) and other tenders do not count; drafts, previews, superseded mails look similar: read each candidate "
    "message. Read selected messages with ONE read_page(urls=[their links], topic '<topic> mail') (read_page also "
    "reads collapsed or locked parts, no need to unlock). Reading pane shows no message text -> use message's own "
    "page link. Skip signing-TAN mails.")

INDEX_JOB = (
    "Search the exact tender reference ALONE (no other word), first inbox then archive. read_page each result "
    "page with topic 'mail index'. On EACH result page, immediately read the matching message links before "
    "moving to another index page or folder; do not spend the entire budget collecting indexes. Prioritize "
    "discount approval and technical release messages from the authorized senders, then other commercial terms. "
    "Use read_page(urls=[observed message links], topic='mail messages'), up to 12 URLs. Return to the observed "
    "index URL to continue pagination. Read all messages for the exact reference, excluding look-alike suffixes, "
    "other tenders and signing TANs. Then done, listing subjects read.\n" + SEARCH_RULES)


@register
class MailScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "mail"
    browser = 3
    max_steps = 24
    hints = ("Adapt to the observed software; these are possible patterns, not requirements. Webmail habits: cookie wall after login; maintenance popups (close them, never follow their links); "
             "search may sit behind slider/robot gate: first try ONE fill_form (slider = its maximum, robot checkbox = "
             "true); still locked -> focus the slider and press End, or click its right end; never loop on evaluate; "
             "inbox and archive folder; paged result lists; message headers "
             "(sender, date) in collapsed 'envelope/headers' section, which read_page includes.")

    async def browse(self, job: str, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("stop_reserve", SUBMIT_RESERVE_S + 150)
        return await super().browse(job, **kwargs)

    async def login(self) -> None:
        try:
            await self.browse("Log in, accept cookie wall, close popups, open inbox. Do NOT search yet. Then done.",
                              max_steps=8)
        except Exception as error:
            self.log.warning("login browse failed: %s", error)

    def topic_jobs(self, facts: dict, covered: set[str]) -> list[str]:
        """One search job per brief topic that has no valid message yet (discount approval first)."""
        senders = dict(facts.get("authorized_senders") or {})
        senders.setdefault("discount_approval", facts.get("director_sender") or "")
        words = dict(facts.get("topic_words") or {})
        words.setdefault("discount_approval", facts.get("discount_topic") or "Rabatt")
        missing = [t for t in dict.fromkeys([*senders, *words]) if t not in covered and t != "signing_tan"]
        missing.sort(key=lambda t: t != "discount_approval")
        jobs = []
        for topic in missing:
            word = words.get(topic) or topic.replace("_", " ")
            sender = senders.get(topic)
            jobs.append(f"Find mails on topic '{word}' ({topic.replace('_', ' ')}) for this tender"
                        f"{f' (sender {sender})' if sender else ''}: search '<reference> {word}' in inbox and "
                        f"archive; read every matching message.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
        return jobs

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            facts, _ = await asyncio.gather(self.wait_brief(), self.login())
            facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or facts
            out = await self.browse_until_done(INDEX_JOB, attempts=2)
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            from agents.analyze_discount import publish
            valid = await publish(self.ctx)
            jobs = self.topic_jobs(facts, covered_topics(valid))
            if jobs and self.ctx.time_left() > 120:
                self.log.info("topics without a valid message: %d searches", len(jobs))
                groups = [jobs[i::TOPIC_TABS] for i in range(min(TOPIC_TABS, len(jobs)))]
                main, rest = groups[0], groups[1:]

                async def in_main() -> None:
                    for job in main:
                        await self.browse_until_done(job, attempts=1, max_steps=16)
                await asyncio.gather(in_main(), self.browse_in_tabs(["\n\n".join(g) for g in rest], attempts=1,
                                                                    max_steps=22))
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail", True)

entries.name: mcp__atira__get_run
entries.description: One run in full: status, phase and failure, its place in the queue or the free models' warm-up while it waits, phase starts on the run's clock, the package, LLM calls by model with failures and queue waits, the score with points per field (test runs), the recordings, the answer it entered, and the run page URL (?t=mm:ss opens the replay there). About 1–2k tokens.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_logs
entries.description: A run's log lines, in time order, each with its time on the run's clock and its stream. Streams: stdout and stderr (your agent system), setup (the platform: install, the free models' warm-up), input (what the browsers received; run_inputs reads them better, so they're left out unless you ask). Narrow with from/to (e.g. from 02:10 to 02:40), grep, browser; tail for the last lines; page with after. About 30 tokens a line.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

stream.description: Only these streams, comma-separated: stdout, stderr, setup, input; "all" is every one. Default: stdout, stderr and setup.

grep.description: Only lines containing this text, case-insensitive; a|b matches either

browser.description: Only the platform's lines about this browser (its inputs, a browser it stopped)

tail.description: Only the last n matching lines

after.description: Continue after a previous page: its `next` value

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `role` ('tender' | 'spec' | 'erp' | 'mail') and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should
find, in general terms derived from the brief; never scenario values). The site id for the role is resolved at run
time (datasets name their sites differently). Override `run()` for several browse passes; call `self.browse(goal)`.

When the scraper ends (done, failed or out of time) it sets results[f"done.{role}"] so analysts waiting on it start.
Independent jobs run at once with `browse_in_tabs` (one new tab each, closed when its job ends); `self.browse` works
in the browser's main tab.
"""
import asyncio

from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import Tab, browse
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
from swarm.extract import brief_intro
from swarm.sites import site_for

ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S = 75     # scrapers stop browsing this long before collecting ends (analysts need the time)


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    role: str = ""
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}
        return f"Site ({self.role}): {site['url']}\nLogin: username {creds.get('username')!r}, password {creds.get('password')!r}"

    def task_text(self) -> str:
        facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or {}
        known = {k: facts.get(k) for k in ("tender_reference", "tender_title", "buyer", "scenario_date", "bidder_company")
                 if facts.get(k)}
        return f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}\nKey facts: {known}" if known else \
            f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        kind = f"{self.role}.page" if rec["kind"] == "page" else rec["kind"]
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=kind, site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"], source=rec["source"],
                                           author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def browse(self, job: str, *, browser: int | None = None, max_steps: int | None = None, **kwargs) -> dict:
        prompt = "\n\n".join([self.login_text(), self.task_text(), f"YOUR JOB:\n{job}"])
        # stop browsing early enough for the analysts to turn the last pages into results before collecting ends
        kwargs.setdefault("stop_reserve", SUBMIT_RESERVE_S + ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S)
        out = await browse(self.ctx, prompt, browser=self.browser if browser is None else browser, site_id=self.site_id,
                           on_record=self.post, max_steps=max_steps or self.max_steps, hints=self.hints,
                           author=self.name, **kwargs)
        self.log.info("browse done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:300])
        return out

    async def browse_until_done(self, job: str, attempts: int = 3, **kwargs) -> dict:
        """browse(); if the agent stopped without finishing (errors, step limit), start again with a note on what
        is already saved, while time allows."""
        out = {"summary": "", "done": False}
        records = []
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            note = ""
            if attempt:
                saved = sorted({e.data.get("topic") for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page")} - {None})
                note = (f"\n\nNOTE: previous attempt stopped early ({out['summary'][:300]!r}). Already saved: "
                        f"{saved or 'nothing'}. Do only what is missing.")
            out = await self.browse(job + note, **kwargs)
            records.extend(out.get("records") or [])
            rejected = self.ctx.shared.get("site_invalidations", {}).get(self.role, set())
            if self.site_id in rejected:
                self.site_id = await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
                # A reused tab may still show the old application; runtime model navigates the newly assigned URL.
                job += "\nThe prior site assignment was contradicted. Navigate to the newly assigned site URL in Login."
                out["done"] = False
            if out["done"] or self.ctx.seconds_left() - kwargs.get("stop_reserve", SUBMIT_RESERVE_S + ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S) < 120:
                break
        return {**out, "records": records}

    async def browse_in_tabs(self, jobs: list[str], *, browser: int | None = None, attempts: int = 2,
                             **kwargs) -> list[dict]:
        """Run `jobs` at once, each in a new tab of this scraper's browser (the tabs share its login cookies). Each tab
        is closed as soon as its job ends, so no tab sits idle. A failed job returns {"summary": error, "done": False}."""
        async def one(job: str) -> dict:
            tab = Tab(self.browser if browser is None else browser)
            try:
                return await self.browse_until_done(job, attempts=attempts, tab=tab, **kwargs)
            except Exception as error:
                self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"tab job failed: {error}")
                return {"summary": str(error), "done": False}
            finally:
                await tab.close()
        return list(await asyncio.gather(*(one(job) for job in jobs)))

    async def wait_brief(self, timeout: float = 180) -> dict:
        try:
            return await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="brief", timeout=timeout) or {}
        except TimeoutError:
            return {}

    def required(self) -> list[tuple[tuple[str, ...], str]]:
        """Pages that must be saved, as (topic keywords, focused job). After the main browse, a focused browse runs
        for each one whose keywords appear in no saved topic. Override per scraper."""
        return []

    def saved_topics(self) -> str:
        return " | ".join(str(e.data.get("topic", "")).lower() for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page"))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            out = await self.browse_until_done(self.goal())   # the brief's intro already names the tender: start at once
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            for keywords, job in self.required():
                if self.ctx.time_left() > 90 and not any(k in self.saved_topics() for k in keywords):
                    self.log.warning("nothing saved for %s: focused browse", keywords)
                    await self.browse(job, max_steps=15)
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"done.{self.role}", True)


def scraper_class(role: str) -> type[SiteScraper] | None:
    from swarm.agent import REGISTRY
    return next((c for c in REGISTRY if isinstance(c, type) and issubclass(c, SiteScraper) and c.role == role), None)


async def run_job(ctx, role: str, job: str, *, max_steps: int = 16, **kwargs) -> dict:
    """One follow-up job on the site of `role`, run by that role's scraper setup (login, hints, browser): in the
    browser's main tab when it is free (logged in already), else in a new tab. For agents/coordinate.py."""
    cls = scraper_class(role)
    if cls is None:
        raise KeyError(f"no scraper for role {role!r}")
    scraper = cls(ctx)
    scraper.name = f"{cls.__name__}.followup"
    scraper.site_id = await site_for(ctx, role)
    main = ctx.lock(f"main_tab.{scraper.browser}")
    if not main.locked():
        async with main:
            return await scraper.browse_until_done(job, attempts=1, max_steps=max_steps, **kwargs)
    return (await scraper.browse_in_tabs([job], attempts=1, max_steps=max_steps, **kwargs))[0]

                        f"{saved or 'nothing'}. Do only what is missing.")

            records.extend(out.get("records") or [])
            rejected = self.ctx.shared.get("site_invalidations", {}).get(self.role, set())

        is closed as soon as its job ends, so no tab sits idle. A failed job returns {"summary": error, "done": False}."""
        async def one(job: str) -> dict:
            tab = Tab(self.browser if browser is None else browser)
            try:

            except Exception as error:

            finally:

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            out = await self.browse_until_done(self.goal())   # the brief's intro already names the tender: start at once
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            for keywords, job in self.required():
                if self.ctx.time_left() > 90 and not any(k in self.saved_topics() for k in keywords):

def scraper_class(role: str) -> type[SiteScraper] | None:
    from swarm.agent import REGISTRY
    return next((c for c in REGISTRY if isinstance(c, type) and issubclass(c, SiteScraper) and c.role == role), None)


async def run_job(ctx, role: str, job: str, *, max_steps: int = 16, **kwargs) -> dict:
    """One follow-up job on the site of `role`, run by that role's scraper setup (login, hints, browser): in the
    browser's main tab when it is free (logged in already), else in a new tab. For agents/coordinate.py."""
    cls = scraper_class(role)
    if cls is None:
        raise KeyError(f"no scraper for role {role!r}")
    scraper = cls(ctx)
    scraper.name = f"{cls.__name__}.followup"
    scraper.site_id = await site_for(ctx, role)
    main = ctx.lock(f"main_tab.{scraper.browser}")
    if not main.locked():

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

async def _browser_ws(cdp_url: str) -> str:
    """The browser's WebSocket debugger URL (CDP_URLS may hold http URLs, as browser-use itself accepts)."""
    if cdp_url.startswith("ws"):
        return cdp_url
    parts = urlparse(cdp_url)
    path = parts.path.rstrip("/")
    path = path if path.endswith("/json/version") else path + "/json/version"
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30) as client:
        reply = await client.get(urlunparse((parts.scheme, parts.netloc, path, "", "", "")))
        return reply.json()["webSocketDebuggerUrl"]


async def _with_cdp(browser: int, call):
    client = CDPClient(await _browser_ws(browsers.cdp_urls()[browser % len(browsers.cdp_urls())]))
    await client.start()
    try:
        return await call(client)
    finally:
        await client.stop()


class Tab:
    """One tab of browser `browser`, owned by one agent (one browse() at a time). `Tab(b)` is a new tab, opened at the
    first browse(); `main_tab(b)` is the tab the browser started with. Locally (no CDP) every browse() starts its own
    Chromium, so a Tab is only a label there."""

    def __init__(self, browser: int, main: bool = False):
        self.browser, self.main = browser, main
        self.target_id: str | None = None
        self.popups: set[str] = set()   # tabs the page opened (window.open, target=_blank) and the agent went into
        self.used = False            # an agent worked here before: the next browse continues from the current page

    def claim(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        self.target_id = target_id
        _OWNERS[target_id] = self

    def adopt(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        """A popup this tab's agent focused: it belongs to this tab from now on (hidden from other agents)."""
        if self.target_id and target_id != self.target_id and owner_of(target_id) in (None, self) \
                and target_id not in _OWNERS:
            _OWNERS[target_id] = self
            self.popups.add(target_id)

    async def open(self) -> None:
        """Create the tab now (before the session connects) so no other agent ever sees it unowned."""
        if self.target_id or self.main or not browsers.cdp_urls():
            return
        # Default: a background tab next to the others in the browser's window, so the live view's tab strip shows every
        # agent (focus emulation keeps typing and focus-dependent scripts working in it; Chrome only slows its timers).
        # TAB_WINDOWS=1: a window per tab instead (always the visible tab there, no timer slowdown, but windows hide
        # each other in the live view).
        params = {"url": "about:blank", "newWindow": True} if os.environ.get("TAB_WINDOWS") == "1" else \
            {"url": "about:blank", "background": True}
        made = await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.createTarget(params=params))
        self.claim(made["targetId"])

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the tab and the popups it adopted (the main tab itself stays open)."""
        targets = list(self.popups) + ([self.target_id] if self.target_id and not self.main else [])

class CdpEndpointRetry(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_dropped_version_request_is_retried(self):
        import httpx
        calls = []

        class Client:
            def __init__(self, **_): pass
            async def __aenter__(self): return self
            async def __aexit__(self, *_): return False
            async def get(self, url):
                calls.append(url)
                if len(calls) == 1:
                    raise httpx.RemoteProtocolError("Server disconnected without sending a response.")
                return httpx.Response(200, json={"webSocketDebuggerUrl": "ws://x/devtools/browser/1"})

        async def no_sleep(_): pass
        with mock.patch.object(ba.httpx, "AsyncClient", Client), mock.patch.object(ba.asyncio, "sleep", no_sleep):
            ws = asyncio.run(ba._browser_ws("http://127.0.0.1:9222"))
        self.assertEqual(ws, "ws://x/devtools/browser/1")
        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 2)
EOF

Progress on run_9dff (about 4 minutes in at the last log): it was hurt by a browser hiccup, not by the new mail code.

**What happened:**
- At 23:39:33 the tender scraper and the mail scraper both crashed in the same second. A hung tab had just been closed, and the request for the browser's debug address got "Server disconnected" back. That request is shared browser code with no retry, and the tender scraper's code is unchanged, so the cause is the browser/sandbox.
- **Consequence:** the board shows 0 positions and the discount missing. The coordinator noticed and listed both as gaps, so follow-up searches may still recover them. Expect a low score for this run unless they do.

**Fixed for the next run** (commit `84284c7` on `kurk-s/mail-topics`, pushed; 153 tests pass):
- The debug-address request now retries twice, after 2 s and 5 s. It's in `swarm/browser_agent.py`, which is CRUBSTERINO's runtime code, so they should know about it.
- One failed mail search now only logs an error, and the other topic searches carry on.

I'm not starting a new test run until this one ends. Its end still shows whether the coordinator fallback works ("jobs straight from the gaps"). The monitor is restarted with a tighter filter: the old one matched every line because of "202" in the timestamps. I'll report the next milestones here.
